decisions.reasoning: Used existing source.yaml as authoritative schema source rather than re-profiling data. This ensures consistency with the approved workload configuration and avoids potential schema drift.

rejection_reasons.from_transformations: Transformations are derived from source schema, not vice versa
rejection_reasons.re_profile: Existing workload is already approved - re-profiling could introduce inconsistencies

alternatives_considered: Only use columns flagged in source.yaml
decisions.choice_made: Map all human-confirmed PII columns with their phi_type and sensitivity from source.yaml
decisions.reasoning: All 8 PII columns in source.yaml (customer_email, customer_phone, credit_card_number, customer_name, shipping_address, city, state, zip_code) were confirmed in the human-provided pii_columns list. Used human confirmation as authoritative rather than auto-detection.

rejection_reasons.auto_detection: Human already provided explicit PII list - auto-detection would be redundant and might flag false positives
rejection_reasons.only_source: Human list matches source.yaml perfectly - both sources agree

decisions.choice_made: Use exact masking methods from approved transformations.yaml
decisions.reasoning: Mapped masking methods from transformations.yaml to semantic.yaml. credit_card_number uses tokenization (most secure for CRITICAL sensitivity), email uses hash (irreversible for HIGH sensitivity), phone/name use mask_partial (balances privacy with usability for MEDIUM-HIGH), addresses use redact (complete removal for MEDIUM sensitivity).

rejection_reasons.all_hash: Different PII types require different masking - one-size-fits-all loses nuance
rejection_reasons.upgrade_encryption: Existing masking strategy is already approved and appropriate for each sensitivity level

alternatives_considered: Move GDPR metadata to separate file
decisions.choice_made: Include full GDPR compliance column metadata in semantic.yaml
decisions.reasoning: GDPR requires explicit tracking of consent, data subject identification, and right-to-erasure. All 5 GDPR compliance columns from transformations.yaml (data_subject_id, consent_given, consent_timestamp, is_deleted, deletion_requested_at) were mapped to semantic.yaml with their business meanings and technical implementations.

rejection_reasons.only_pii: GDPR compliance requires more than just PII identification - needs consent tracking and erasure flags
rejection_reasons.separate_file: Semantic.yaml is the single source of truth for all column metadata - splitting would reduce discoverability

decisions.reasoning: Categorized 18 columns into 5 roles: 4 measures (revenue, quantity, unit_price, discount_pct), 2 dimensions (payment_method, order_status), 2 temporal (order_date, ship_date), 3 identifiers (order_id, customer_id, product_id), 8 PII, and 5 GDPR compliance. This categorization enables proper aggregation semantics and query generation.

rejection_reasons.flat_list: Role categorization is essential for semantic layer query generation - flat list loses aggregation semantics
rejection_reasons.numeric_only: Too coarse - doesn't capture temporal vs identifier distinction

alternatives_considered: Manual validation instead of automated tests
decisions.choice_made: Comprehensive test coverage across validation, consistency, and compliance dimensions
decisions.reasoning: Created 25 unit tests (schema validation, required fields, PII flagging, encryption config) and 19 integration tests (cross-config consistency, column mappings, GDPR compliance, quality rule validation). Integration tests validate that all configs reference the same entities correctly.

rejection_reasons.manual_validation: Manual validation is error-prone and not repeatable - automated tests catch regressions
rejection_reasons.only_semantic: Metadata spans 4 config files (source, semantic, transformations, quality) - must test consistency across all

alternatives_considered: Use SUM for all numeric columns
decisions.choice_made: Use SUM for additive measures, AVG for rates and unit values
decisions.reasoning: Assigned default_aggregation to each measure: SUM for revenue/quantity (additive metrics), AVG for unit_price/discount_pct (averaging prices/rates makes sense, summing them does not). This guides semantic layer query generation to produce correct SQL.

rejection_reasons.sum_all: Summing unit_price or discount_pct produces meaningless values - AVG is correct
rejection_reasons.unspecified: Semantic layer needs aggregation hints - without them, default SUM could produce nonsense (summed prices)

revenue is derived column: quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount_pct), rounded to 2 decimals
Timezone is America/New_York for all date operations and scheduling
